properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Wish 15 from the dev_storyflow agent, 2026-09-04.

THEIR ATTEMPT, and it is a complete enumeration of what the schema offers: "`SUPERSEDES` REFUSED Decision→Decision. `OBSOLETES` was allowed BUT WOULD HAVE SET `discontinued: true` on the older node, which was wrong — THE OLDER DECISION WAS STILL LIVE, JUST NARROWER. I used `CONTRADICTS` with evidence, WHICH READS AS A FIGHT RATHER THAN A REFINEMENT."

CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: `schema/build.yaml:133` declares SUPERSEDES as `from: [Fragment, Verification]`, `to: [Fragment, Verification]` — Decision is not in either list, so the refusal is the schema working as written.

⭐ SO ALL THREE AVAILABLE EDGES ASSERT SOMETHING FALSE. `SUPERSEDES` is unavailable; `OBSOLETES` says the older ruling is WITHDRAWN when it is still governing; `CONTRADICTS` says the two CANNOT BOTH HOLD when in fact both hold and one is a special case of the other. The reporter took the third and flagged it themselves — which is the honest move and still leaves a false claim in the graph, readable by `detect_defects` as a design inconsistency.

THE SHAPE HAS A NAME IN EVERY OTHER DISCIPLINE. A later ruling that narrows an earlier one without repealing it is the ordinary way a body of decisions grows. reflow2 models WITHDRAWAL and CONFLICT and has no word for REFINEMENT.

DIRECTIONS, none chosen:
① OPEN `SUPERSEDES` TO Decision→Decision. Cheapest, and wrong for their case by their own account: supersede still reads as replacement, and the older decision was not replaced.
② A NEW EDGE — `NARROWS` / `REFINES`. Says the true thing. ⚠️ New vocabulary is the expensive answer and this project's own bar is that a distinction must be READ by something, not merely stated. What would read it? `what_next`'s shaping band, and any walk that asks "which rulings govern here" — both of which today would show the older decision alone.
③ A PROPERTY ON `CONTRADICTS`, e.g. `alignment: narrowing` beside the existing `opposing`. ⭐ THE CHEAPEST HONEST ONE: the reporter already used `CONTRADICTS` with `alignment` set, so the field exists and the edge is drawn — this only stops the detector reading a refinement as a defect.
④ NOTHING, AND SAY SO. Prose in the newer decision names the older; the graph stays silent. That is what happened, and it is the state that produced the report.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how common this is. n=1 here. But reflow2's own graph holds 232 open decisions and several chains where a later idea plainly narrows an earlier one — nobody has counted how many are currently joined by nothing, or by a `CONTRADICTS` that overstates.
properties.name: OPEN — "this ruling sharpens that one" is a normal relation between decisions and has no edge; the three available ones each assert something false
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill; recorded as an idea. Kept separate from the revision-layers idea even though both came from the same session and the same node: this one is about the relation BETWEEN two decisions, that one about the history WITHIN one field, and a fix to either leaves the other exactly where it was.
